newsitem.title: USA: US sees no rush for WTO pact with China-Barshefsky.
newsitem.headline: US sees no rush for WTO pact with China-Barshefsky.

text.p: The United States will not be rushed into reaching an agreement with China on that country's entry into the World Trade Organisation, U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said on Wednesday.
"There's no race here," despite the pressure of the upcoming summit between President Bill Clinton and Chinese President Jiang Zemin here in October, Barshefsky told reporters.
The only important issue is that whatever agreement is reached "is going to have to be very, very good," she said.

In recent days, Barshefsky and other administration aides have noted that China's offers so far have fallen short of what is needed for it to join the World Trade Organisation, which governs trade for most of the world.

But some progress has been made in the talks, Barshefsky said. For example, China has pledged not to subsidise agricultural exports, which is very important because of its huge productive capacity, she said.
China does not currently subsidise farm exports. But "there was a growing concern" that China could use export subsidies in future years to break into foreign markets, she said.
Meanwhile, the White House said on Wednesday that Clinton's national security advisor Sandy Berger will travel to Beijing next week for pre-summit talks.

"He'll meet with Jiang and other Chinese leaders to continue the strategic dialogue that we began last year," White House spokeswoman Anne Luzzatto said. Those talks cover "a broad range of issues," she said.
At this point, "there would have to be more on the table than there is now" for top U.S. trade officials to travel to Beijing, Barshefsky said.
But the United States expects China to make new offers on tariffs and services in the WTO talks in late August or early September, she said.

Progress could still come quickly if China decides it wants to move forward, Barshefsky said. "I don't think we can prejudge one way or another" whether an agreement can be reached by the October summit, she said.
